title: Move the install's secrets into its Key Vault
purpose: Moves the secrets of one PIM Manager install that are not Key Vault references -- Container Apps secrets stored as values and plain container settings that hold a secret -- into the install's own Key Vault, and switches each app and job to a Key Vault reference read with its own identity.
whenToRun: Once per install with -GrantOnly, when the setup step 'Secrets only in Key Vault' (keyvault-secrets-only) says the Support app must act: it grants the updater and the readers their Key Vault rights, and the install's updater moves the secrets in its next update run. By hand (plan first, then -Apply) only where the updater cannot.

runAs.name: Contributor (or Container Apps Contributor)
runAs.why: Reads the container apps and jobs, reads their secrets (listSecrets) and switches their secret definitions (a new revision of the Manager app).

runAs.name: User Access Administrator (or Role Based Access Control Administrator)
runAs.why: Creates the Azure role assignment Key Vault Secrets User for the identities that read the moved secrets, at the vault only.

runAs.name: Key Vault Secrets Officer
runAs.why: Writes each moved value as a vault secret and reads it back to compare (by SHA-256; the value is never printed).

changes.object: one secret per moved value, named <app or job>-<secret> (an existing secret with the same value is reused, no new version)
changes.scope: the install's own Key Vault (-VaultName, or the one vault of the resource group; Azure RBAC authorization required)
changes.why: Secrets live in Key Vault only (framework 4). The value is written, read back and compared by SHA-256 before anything is switched.
changes.undo: Disable or delete the vault secret -- only after the app / job was switched back (see the rollback record).

changes.object: the user-assigned identity id-pim-<role> of each app / job whose secret moves (engine, web, updater, docs, downlink only)
changes.scope: the install's own Key Vault at resource scope (/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>) -- never the resource group or the subscription
changes.why: Container Apps reads a Key Vault reference with that identity. An existing assignment at the vault is left alone; it is read back before any switch.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignment on the vault (Azure portal > key vault > Access control), after switching the app / job back.

changes.object: with -GrantOnly (the Support-app grant step): the updater job's own user-assigned identity id-pim-updater
changes.permission: Key Vault Secrets Officer (Azure role b86a8fe4-44ce-4948-aee5-eccb2c155cd7)
changes.scope: the install's own Key Vault at resource scope -- never the resource group or the subscription
changes.why: The install's own updater writes the secrets into the vault and switches the apps and jobs inside its update run; the updater may not assign roles itself, so the Support app grants this once.
changes.undo: Remove the role assignment on the vault (Azure portal > key vault > Access control); the updater's step then reports the right missing and moves nothing.

changes.object: each moved secret of a container app / job becomes keyVaultUrl + identity; each plain setting that held a secret becomes a secretRef to a new Key Vault referenced secret; every other secret and setting is kept
changes.scope: the install's container apps and jobs (-Only limits them); the Manager app gets a new revision, a job applies it to its next execution
changes.why: No secret value left in an app or job definition. Read back; a failed read-back puts the previous definitions back.
changes.undo: The rollback record (JSON, no values) lists the previous definitions and the steps: read the value from its vault secret and set the app / job secret back to a value (ARM PATCH).

changes.object: the plan and the rollback record (JSON, names only -- never a value) in -LogDir
changes.why: What was planned and done, and how to switch back.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The subscription of the PIM install (always explicit).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The resource group of the PIM install (its container apps, jobs and Key Vault).

parameters.name: VaultName
parameters.help: The install's own Key Vault; it must be in -ResourceGroup and use Azure RBAC authorization.

parameters.name: Only
parameters.help: Limit the move to these app / job names.

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.help: Move. Without it the script only plans (read-only).

parameters.name: GrantOnly
parameters.help: The Support-app grant step: Key Vault Secrets Officer for the updater (id-pim-updater) and Key Vault Secrets User for each identity that reads a secret to move, at the vault only, read back. No secret is read, written or switched -- the updater moves them in its next update run.

parameters.name: WaitForIdleRuns
parameters.help: Switch a job only when none of its executions runs (waits at most -IdleWaitMinutes, then that job is deferred; nothing is ever stopped).

parameters.name: RbacWaitSeconds
parameters.help: Wait this long after a NEW role assignment before the first switch (a new assignment takes a while to reach Container Apps).

parameters.name: LogDir
parameters.default: a folder under the temp folder
parameters.help: Where the plan and the rollback record are written as JSON.

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: Sign in as yourself in the browser, or use the Invardia Support session open in this window. No command-line tool, no module.

parameters.name: AdminAppId
parameters.help: Automation: the admin application's client id (with -AdminCertThumbprint).

parameters.name: AdminCertThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation: the thumbprint of the admin application's certificate in the local machine store.

readsOnly: the install's container apps and jobs (their secret names, Key Vault references, identities and settings; the plan never reads a value)
the install's Key Vaults (which one, Azure RBAC authorization) and the role assignments at the vault
with -Apply: the secret values (Container Apps listSecrets), held in memory only, and the vault secrets to compare by SHA-256
whatIf: Signs in and reads, and prints the plan with names only: 'What if: would MOVE secret <name> (a value in the app definition) -> vault secret <app>-<name> -> keyVaultUrl ... + identity id-pim-<role>', 'What if: would MOVE env <container>/<NAME> (a plain value) -> ...', 'What if: would GRANT Key Vault Secrets User (4633458b-...) to id-pim-<role> ... at /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault> (resource scope: the vault only)', the effect per app / job (new revision / next execution) and with -Apply the steps as 'would'. Nothing is written in Azure; the plan file (names only) is written locally.
undo: Follow the rollback record: for each app / job set the moved secrets back to values (read each from its vault secret) and the moved settings back to plain values, then optionally remove the Key Vault Secrets User assignments at the vault and the vault secrets.
